stem: An object is said to be in motion if its __________ changes with time relative to a reference point.
solution: Motion is a change in the position of an object with time relative to a reference point.

stem: The total path length covered by an object is called the __________.
solution: Distance is the total length of the path travelled by an object, a scalar quantity.

stem: The shortest straight-line distance from the initial to the final position, with direction, is the __________.
solution: Displacement is the shortest distance from start to finish with direction, a vector quantity.

stem: A quantity that has only magnitude is called a __________ quantity.
solution: A scalar quantity has magnitude only, e.g., distance and speed.

stem: A quantity that has both magnitude and direction is called a __________ quantity.
solution: A vector quantity has both magnitude and direction, e.g., displacement and velocity.

stem: The distance travelled by an object per unit time is its __________.
solution: Speed is the distance covered per unit time; it is a scalar.

stem: The displacement of an object per unit time is its __________.
solution: Velocity is the rate of change of displacement — it has direction, making it a vector.

stem: The SI unit of speed and velocity is __________.
solution: Speed and velocity are measured in metres per second (m/s).

stem: The rate of change of velocity of an object is called its __________.
solution: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity with time.

stem: The SI unit of acceleration is __________.
solution: Acceleration is measured in metres per second squared (m/s²).

stem: When the velocity of an object decreases with time, the acceleration is __________.
solution: A decreasing velocity means negative acceleration, also called retardation or deceleration.

stem: An object moving with constant velocity has an acceleration of __________.
solution: Constant velocity means no change in velocity, so acceleration is zero.

stem: Uniform motion is motion in which an object covers __________ in equal intervals of time.
solution: In uniform motion, equal distances are covered in equal time intervals (constant speed).

stem: In non-uniform motion, an object covers __________ in equal intervals of time.
solution: In non-uniform motion, the speed changes, so unequal distances are covered in equal time intervals.

stem: On a distance–time graph, uniform motion is represented by a __________.
solution: Uniform speed gives a straight, sloping line on a distance–time graph.

stem: On a distance–time graph, an object at rest is shown by a __________.
solution: An object at rest keeps the same position, so its distance–time graph is a horizontal line.

stem: The slope of a distance–time graph gives the __________.
solution: The slope (gradient) of a distance–time graph gives the speed of the object.

stem: On a velocity–time graph, the slope gives the __________.
solution: The slope of a velocity–time graph gives the acceleration.

stem: On a velocity–time graph, the area under the graph gives the __________.
solution: The area under a velocity–time graph gives the distance (or displacement) travelled.

stem: The first equation of motion is __________ (for uniform acceleration).
solution: The first equation of motion is v = u + at, where u is initial velocity, a is acceleration, t is time.

stem: The second equation of motion is __________.
solution: The second equation of motion is s = ut + ½at², giving displacement s.

stem: The third equation of motion is __________.
solution: The third equation of motion is v² = u² + 2as, relating velocity and displacement.

stem: A car starting from rest and reaching 20 m/s in 4 s has an acceleration of __________.
A body moving at 10 m/s covers a distance of __________ in 5 s (uniform speed).
solution: Distance = speed × time = 10 × 5 = 50 m.

stem: The average speed of an object is the __________.
options: total distance divided by total time
solution: Average speed = total distance travelled ÷ total time taken.

stem: Motion in a circle at constant speed is an example of __________ motion.
solution: In uniform circular motion, the direction of velocity constantly changes, so the motion is accelerated.

stem: A body moving in a circular path with constant speed has changing __________.
solution: Its speed is constant but its direction (hence velocity) keeps changing, so it is accelerating.

stem: The distance covered by an object can be __________ its displacement.
solution: Distance is always greater than or equal to the magnitude of displacement.

stem: If an object returns to its starting point, its displacement is __________.
solution: When an object returns to its start, its net displacement is zero, though the distance is not.

stem: A runner completes one full round of a 400 m circular track, returning to the start. Their distance and displacement are respectively __________.
solution: The distance is 400 m (path length); the displacement is 0 (starts and ends at the same point).

stem: A velocity–time graph that is a horizontal straight line shows __________.
solution: A horizontal line on a velocity–time graph shows constant velocity, so acceleration is zero.

stem: The gradient (steepness) of a velocity–time graph that slopes upward indicates __________.
solution: An upward slope on a velocity–time graph indicates positive (increasing) acceleration.

stem: For an object in free fall (ignoring air resistance), the acceleration is due to __________.
solution: A freely falling object accelerates due to gravity, about 9.8 m/s² near the Earth's surface.

stem: The speedometer of a car shows its __________.
solution: A speedometer shows the instantaneous speed of a vehicle at a given moment.

stem: A change from 30 km/h to 30 m/s uses the conversion 1 m/s = __________ km/h.
solution: 1 m/s = 3.6 km/h (multiply m/s by 3.6 to get km/h).

stem: 72 km/h expressed in m/s is __________.
Which of the following is a vector quantity?
solution: Velocity has both magnitude and direction (a vector); speed, distance and time are scalars.

stem: Which of the following is a scalar quantity?
solution: Distance is a scalar (magnitude only); the others are vectors.

stem: An object moving with increasing speed in a straight line has __________.
solution: Increasing speed in a straight line means positive acceleration.

stem: The reference point chosen to describe the position of an object is called the __________.
solution: Motion is described relative to a chosen reference point or origin.

stem: Motion is said to be relative because it depends on the __________.
solution: Whether an object is moving or at rest depends on the chosen reference frame — motion is relative.

stem: A passenger sitting in a moving train is at rest relative to __________.
solution: The passenger is at rest relative to the train but in motion relative to the ground and trees.

stem: The area under a velocity–time graph for uniform motion is a __________ shape.
solution: For uniform (constant) velocity, the velocity–time graph is horizontal, so the area under it is a rectangle.

stem: A car covers the first half of a journey at high speed and the second at low speed; its motion is __________.
solution: Changing speed during the journey means the motion is non-uniform.

stem: The acceleration of an object thrown straight up (while going up) is __________.
solution: Gravity acts downward, so a ball thrown up decelerates, with acceleration directed downward.

stem: Two cars travel the same distance; the one taking less time has a __________ average speed.
solution: For the same distance, less time means a higher average speed.

stem: If the velocity–time graph is a straight line passing through the origin sloping upward, the object has __________.
solution: A straight sloping line from the origin means uniform acceleration starting from rest.

stem: The distance–time graph of a uniformly accelerating object (starting from rest) is a __________.
solution: For uniform acceleration, distance increases faster with time, giving a curve that gets steeper.

stem: A body moving with uniform velocity has __________ acceleration.
solution: Uniform velocity means no change in velocity, so acceleration is zero.

stem: The magnitude of displacement is always __________ the distance travelled.
solution: Displacement is always less than or equal to the distance travelled.

stem: The overall message of the chapter 'Describing Motion Around Us' is that:
options: motion is described using distance, displacement, speed, velocity and acceleration, and represented by graphs and equations of motion
speed and velocity are the same
solution: The chapter describes motion using scalar and vector quantities (distance, displacement, speed, velocity, acceleration), graphs, and the equations of motion.

stem: The change in position of an object with time is called __________.
solution: Motion is the change in the position of an object with respect to time.

stem: The actual length of the path travelled by an object is called __________.
solution: Distance is the total path length covered, a scalar quantity.

stem: The shortest straight-line distance between the initial and final positions is called __________.
solution: Displacement is the shortest distance from start to finish, with direction (a vector).

stem: The distance travelled per unit time is called __________.
solution: Speed is the distance covered per unit time, a scalar.

stem: The SI unit of speed is __________.
solution: The SI unit of speed is metre per second (m/s).

stem: The rate of change of displacement is called __________.
solution: Velocity is the rate of change of displacement, a vector.

stem: The rate of change of velocity is called __________.
solution: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity with time.

stem: If the velocity of an object decreases with time, its acceleration is called __________.
solution: Decreasing velocity means negative acceleration, also called retardation or deceleration.

stem: An object moving with a constant velocity has __________ acceleration.
solution: Constant velocity means no change in velocity, so acceleration is zero.

stem: Uniform motion means an object covers __________ distances in equal intervals of time.
solution: In uniform motion, equal distances are covered in equal time intervals.

stem: In a distance-time graph, a straight line indicates __________ motion.
solution: A straight-line distance-time graph indicates uniform (constant-speed) motion.

stem: The slope of a distance-time graph gives the __________.
solution: The slope of a distance-time graph gives the speed of the object.

stem: The slope of a velocity-time graph gives the __________.
solution: The slope of a velocity-time graph gives acceleration.

stem: The area under a velocity-time graph gives the __________.
solution: The area under a velocity-time graph gives the distance/displacement covered.

stem: The first equation of motion is __________.
solution: The first equation of motion relating velocity, acceleration and time is v = u + at.

stem: Motion of an object in a circular path at constant speed is called __________ circular motion.
solution: Uniform circular motion is motion in a circle at constant speed.

stem: Even at constant speed, circular motion is accelerated because the __________ changes continuously.
solution: In circular motion the direction of velocity changes, so it is accelerated.

stem: The state of rest and motion are __________.
solution: Rest and motion are relative; they depend on the reference point (observer).

stem: An object thrown vertically upward experiences an acceleration due to __________.
solution: Gravity acts downward, decelerating the rising object and accelerating it as it falls.

stem: The value of acceleration due to gravity near the Earth's surface is about __________.
solution: The acceleration due to gravity is about 9.8 m/s² near the Earth's surface.

stem: The odometer of a vehicle measures the __________ travelled.
solution: An odometer records the total distance travelled by a vehicle.

stem: The speedometer of a vehicle indicates the __________.
solution: A speedometer shows the instantaneous speed of the vehicle.

stem: The total distance divided by the total time gives the __________ speed.
solution: Average speed is total distance divided by total time.

stem: A body has uniform acceleration if its velocity changes by __________ amounts in equal time intervals.
solution: Uniform acceleration means velocity changes by equal amounts in equal times.

stem: The distance-time graph for a stationary object is a __________.
solution: For a stationary object, distance does not change with time, giving a horizontal line.

stem: Two objects are said to be in relative motion if their positions change with respect to __________.
solution: Relative motion is a change in position of objects with respect to each other.
